surface_verification.justification: backfill_phase_tasks.py is a CLI tool run against an already-adopted project's shipwright_run_config.json; it has no web/dev-server surface of its own to browser-verify. Effective complexity is small (not medium+), so F0.5 is not mandatory -- verification is the unit/integration test suite (F0) plus a manual --dry-run against the real live leadwright repo, documented in the ADR's Confidence Calibration section.

behaviors.behavior: AC1: an adopted config written before this campaign (has completed_steps, no phase_tasks[]) reads correctly after the backfill
AC2: the backfill is idempotent -- running it twice changes nothing
AC3: verified against a real pre-existing adopted config, not only a synthetic fixture
behaviors.evidence: test_backfill_phase_tasks_cli.py::test_backfills_the_real_leadwright_config PASSED (verbatim copy of the live leadwright shipwright_run_config.json) + manual --dry-run against the actual C:\01_Development\leadwright checkout, confirmed byte-identical before/after (documented in the ADR; no unattended write to a sibling repo)

behaviors.behavior: a phase_tasks value that is present but malformed (not a list) is left entirely untouched, never overwritten
duplicate completed_steps entries produce only one phase_tasks entry per phase
adoption: null does not crash the backfill, resolves to not-applicable
a non-adopted (driven, not adopted) config is reported not-applicable and left byte-untouched
an out-of-vocabulary completed_steps entry is skipped, not fatal
when phase_tasks[] already partially exists, only the gap is filled -- existing entries are never duplicated or rewritten
a BOM-prefixed config (Notepad-style save) is read, not rejected
behaviors.evidence: test_backfill_phase_tasks_cli.py::test_a_bom_prefixed_config_is_read_not_rejected PASSED (confidence calibration probe finding, fixed via utf-8-sig)

behaviors.behavior: CRLF line endings and non-ASCII field values round-trip cleanly
backfilled entries carry the original adoption timestamp, not the backfill run's own time
a backfilled phase's status agrees with what phase_history already recorded for it (e.g. 'test' backfills as skipped, matching history)
the pure backfill function never mutates its input dict in place
the shared handoff pipeline renders no compliance-dashboard 'skipped' block for a backfilled pre-s2 config
the shared has_phase_tasks() reader treats a backfilled pre-s2 config the same as a freshly-adopted (post-s2) one
